title: Harmony in the band and picking tempos
summary: New Orleans bands had no dissension and chose whatever tempo made a number work.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: The same way, then the next thing about it, there was no dissension in the band. Everybody was happy. Just one big family. When they played the job, everybody was glad to play the job. They loved music, and they loved each other. They liked to play together. And they had one distinct style of putting over their music. They rehearsed the number. If the number was written slow, they'd play it as it was written. And if it didn't sound good to the band in that slow tempo, they'd pick up the tempo. And if it sounded better in the fastest tempo, that's the way they played it.
